questions.paper_title: Hard but Robust, Easy but Sensitive: How Encoder and Decoder Perform in Neural Machine Translation
questions.question: How do they determine that a decoder handles an easier task than the encoder?

references.answer: adding more layers to the encoder achieves larger improvements than adding more layers to the decoder, the decoder converges faster than the encoder
evidence: The decoder handles an easier task than the encoder. 1) We find that adding more layers to the encoder achieves larger improvements than adding more layers to the decoder. 2) We also compare the training time of the encoder and decoder by fixing the parameters of a well-trained decoder (encoder), and just update the parameters of the encoder (decoder). We found that the decoder converges faster than the encoder. These two results suggest that the decoder handles an easier task than the encoder in NMT.
